rationale: The expression matches the stated hypothesis and the level-minus-volatility cash-flow leg is a defensible conditioning variable, but the signal is essentially R&D-intensity (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) crossed with a cash-flow quality/low-volatility screen, so novelty is modest and the true test is whether the interaction adds anything beyond the additive legs.

This is the most mechanical possible cross of two heavily published anomalies — R&D+advertising-to-sales and Novy-Marx gross-profits-to-assets — with no conditioning logic that a simple double sort on the two known factors would not already capture.

Dividing earnings by COALESCE'd intangibles plus goodwill creates a near-zero/zero denominator for the majority of firms, so the ratio explodes or drops out and the cross-sectional ranking will be driven by intangible-asset scarcity rather than the claimed earnings persistence on intangible capital.

Same denominator degeneracy problem (intan + 5-year R&D sum is zero for many firms, biasing coverage toward R&D-intensive names), and the second leg is simply a book-equity-minus-leverage ratio, making the composite a repackaging of intangible-capital turnover (Peters-Taylor/Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou) times low leverage.

Internally consistent (high intangible ramp × high cash-flow volatility/leverage → negative expected sign) and the fragility conditioning is a genuinely different angle from standard investment-growth anomalies, though GROWTH on a ratio whose base is often zero will generate outliers and the multiplicative form conflates low-growth firms with robust ones.

Both legs are published constructs (accumulated intangible/organization capital intensity and retained-earnings-to-book-equity à la Ball et al.), the product adds no new economic conditioning, and re/ceq is unstable for firms with small or negative book equity.
